title: Berlin Defence (3...Nf6)
intro: Against the solid Berlin Defence, play 4.d3 to avoid forced endgame trades and enjoy a rich middlegame with c3 and O-O.
variation: e2e4 e7e5 g1f3 b8c6 f1b5 g8f6

lessons.title: The Anti-Berlin with 4.d3
lessons.summary: Keep queens on with 4.d3, then build c3 and O-O.

steps.text: With 3...Nf6, Black plays the Berlin Defence, attacking e4 and aiming to trade queens after 4.O-O Nxe4.
Keep the queens on the board and defend e4 solidly.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4.d3: it defends e4 and keeps a full middlegame ahead.
steps.ifRight: Now White threatens Bxc6 followed by Nxe5.

feedback.e1g1: 4.O-O is the main line, leading to the sharp Berlin Endgame after 4...Nxe4 5.d4 Nd6. 4.d3 is simpler and very strong.

steps.text: Give your bishop a retreat square and prepare to push d4 later.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.c3 to prepare d4 and Ba4-c2.
steps.ifRight: Your Spanish bishop is safe and White plans O-O and Nbd2.
White is castled with clear plans.

steps.text: Black defends e5 with 6...d6. Continue developing.
steps.hint: Develop your queen's knight or stop ...Bg4 with h3.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7.Nbd2 (or 7.h3 or 7.Bg5) to bring your pieces into the game.
steps.ifRight: White plans Re1, Nf1 and Ng3, just like in the Closed Ruy Lopez.

lessons.title: Meeting 4...d6
lessons.summary: Play c3 and O-O, and avoid the ...c6 and ...Qa5+ trap.

steps.text: Instead of 4...Bc5, Black may play solidly with 4...d6.
Prepare d4 and give your b5 bishop a square on c2.
steps.ifRight: White controls d4 and keeps the bishop safe.

steps.text: Black prepares a kingside fianchetto with 5...g6.

steps.ifRight: Now White develops Nbd2 and Re1.

steps.text: Careful if Black tries 4...Ne7, hoping you take on e5 and walk into ...c6 and ...Qa5+.
Do not fall for the ...c6 and ...Qa5+ fork. Keep developing.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.O-O (or 5.c3): taking on e5 loses to 5...c6 6.Bc4 Qa5+.
steps.ifRight: Safe and strong: if Black plays ...c6 now, Ba4 keeps a great diagonal.

feedback.f3e5: 5.Nxe5 walks into 5...c6 6.Bc4 Qa5+ and 7...Qxe5, losing a piece.

lessons.title: Tactics in the Anti-Berlin
lessons.summary: Retreat Ba4-b3, answer ...Bg4 with h3, and punish premature ...d5 breaks.

steps.text: Black often asks your bishop what it wants with 7...a6.
Keep your Spanish bishop on the active diagonal.
steps.ifWrong: Play 8.Ba4 so the bishop can later swing to c2.
steps.ifRight: If Black pushes ...b5, Bb3 keeps the bishop aiming at f7.

steps.text: Black opens space on the queenside with 8...b5.
Retreat one more square to the b3 diagonal.
steps.ifRight: White is ready for Re1, Nf1 and Ng3.

steps.text: Black pins your knight with 9...Bg4. How should White break the pin and route the knight?
steps.hint: Question the g4 bishop with h3 or prepare Nf1 with Re1.
steps.ifWrong: Play 10.h3 (or 10.Re1): after 10...Bh5, 11.Re1 Nf1 Ng3 puts pressure on h5.
steps.ifRight: If 10...Bh5, White follows with Re1, Nf1 and Ng3, winning time against the bishop.

steps.text: Black pushes 8...d5 early. Take advantage of the open centre.
steps.hint: Capture on d5 or pin the f6 knight.
steps.ifWrong: Play 9.exd5 (or 9.Bg5) to win space and pressure e5.
steps.ifRight: After 9.exd5 Nxd5 10.Re1, e5 is under strong pressure.
